status_effects.explanation: She privately registers the anecdote about an evening she was left out of as a perfidious dig.
She recovers the upper hand by capping the anecdote with her own superior version of the same story.
Her boastful anecdote about Ristori's visit is quietly deflated when Mme de Villeparisis tops it with a superior version of the same anecdote.

appraisal_events.evidence: « si j'avais su que vous n'aviez votre soirée prise par personne, je vous aurais envoyé chercher... c'était d'une beauté ! » / « Quelle perfidie ! pensa Mme de Villeparisis. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The interlocutor's anecdote about a brilliant impromptu evening at her own house, to which Mme de Villeparisis was pointedly not invited, is read by Mme de Villeparisis as a veiled slight, though this reading is entirely filtered through her own suspicious free-indirect thought rather than confirmed by the narrator.

appraisal_events.evidence: « J'ai entendu Mme Ristori dans son beau temps, ce n'est plus qu'une ruine. Et puis je déteste les vers de Carmen Sylva. La Ristori est venue ici une fois... dire un chant de l'Enfer, de Dante. Voilà où elle est incomparable. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Villeparisis deflates the interlocutor's boast by dismissing Ristori's present talent and Carmen Sylva's verses, then trumps the story with her own superior memory of Ristori performing Dante at her own house, quietly undercutting the other woman's implied social edge.

ambiguities: The speaker of the 'Ma chère, Mme de Luynes me fait penser à Yolande...' line is not explicitly tagged as the duchesse de Guermantes within this excerpt; the attribution follows the candidate list but is not textually certain from the passage alone.
